You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H5749b

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "To testify, warn, or solemnly charge; also to call or summon as witness"
  Readable gloss: "Derived from the root for 'witness,' this Hiphil verb operates across a spectrum from solemn warning to formal testimony to the causative act of establishing witnesses. When God 'warned' Israel through the prophets (2 Kgs 17:13), the urgency is paramount; when Naboth's accusers 'testified against' him (1 Kgs 21:13), the juridical sense dominates. Moses 'calls heaven and earth to witness' (Deut 4:26; 30:19) in a third, causative use that invokes cosmic accountability. French often flattens all three into 'avertir,' while Spanish distinguishes 'advertir' (warn) from 'testificar' (testify)."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "warn, admonish, charge"
    Enriched: The most common use: solemn warning or admonishment, often with prophetic urgency. Genesis 43:3 has Joseph's stern charge, and Exodus 19:21, 23 records God commanding Moses to warn the people. Spanish 'advertir/amonestar' and French 'avertir' capture the admonitory force. The emphasis falls on preventing wrongdoing or disaster through authoritative speech.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-advertí, Y-advirtió, Y-amonestó, Y-testificaste, advertir, advertiste, advertí, advierte, nos-advirtió, os-he-advertido, testificaron, y-advertí, y-advirtiendo, y-amonestaré, y-fue-advertido, y-les-amonestaron, y-te-advertí, y-testificaste
  Sense 2: "testify, bear witness"
    Enriched: Formal testimony or witness-bearing, whether for or against someone. In 1 Kings 21:10, 13, false witnesses 'testify against' Naboth; in Job 29:11, the ear that heard Job 'testified in his favor.' Deuteronomy 8:19 combines warning with testimony: 'I testify against you today.' Spanish 'testificar' and the juridical framing in Kings highlight the courtroom register of this sense.
    Existing Spanish translations: testificaré-de-ti?, testificaste, testifico, testificó, y-testificaba-de-mí, y-testificaron-contra-él, y-testificaré, y-testifiquen, y-testifiquen-contra-él
  Sense 3: "call or summon as witness"
    Enriched: The causative act of summoning or establishing witnesses -- making someone or something serve as testimony. Moses 'calls heaven and earth as witnesses' (Deut 4:26; 30:19; 31:28), and Jeremiah summons human witnesses to a deed (Jer 32:10). Spanish 'llamar por testigos' and 'tomar como testigos' clearly convey the causative Hiphil force of causing others to stand as witnesses.
    Existing Spanish translations: Y-tomaré-como-testigos, e-hice-testificar, llamo-por-testigos, pongo-por-testigos, y-haciendo-testificar, y-haz-testificar, y-llamaré-por-testigos
